name: ambiguous
title: Ambiguous: "make it safer and handle more traffic" with a mid-run requirement change
requirement: People are abusing the shortener. Make it safer, make sure it can handle more traffic, and the analytics should be better.
narrative: The analyst refuses to guess: vague terms become clarification questions with proposed defaults; the product owner answers one explicitly (30 creates/minute) and accepts the rest as recorded assumptions. Scale and analytics work are explicitly deferred. A host-configuration change (Program.cs) is routed to a tech lead by change-control policy. After the first build the product owner changes the requirement (rate-limit redirects too): only affected nodes go stale, the planner's previous expansion is retracted and its changes compensated, a new plan (graph v+1) is executed, and the earlier clarification is formally superseded.

approvals.comment: Framework rate limiter acceptable; WAF-level limits tracked as follow-up.
Program.cs change reviewed: UseRateLimiter placement is correct.

externalEvents.content: People are abusing the shortener. Make it safer, make sure it can handle more traffic, and the analytics should be better. UPDATE from the product owner: scrapers are hammering popular short links, so rate limiting must apply to redirects as well.
externalEvents.reason: Requirement changed mid-run: redirect scraping observed in production.
